usual_baseline: Time and pressure are usually recorded (time 56–95%, pressure 20.5–88%). Skin condition, isolation and exsanguination are almost never recorded: 0–43%. Pressures often exceed BOAST limits: within standard in only 24–35% in two audits, over in 47.5–70% in another. Fixed 250 mmHg used in 95.3% [2602]. Time over 120 minutes is rare.
fix_that_works: A mandatory electronic op note template: skin 37% to 69%, pressure documented 71% to 94%, within limit 25% to 75% [1650]. EPR auto-text: skin 0% to 64.3%, exsanguination 5.6% to 42.9% [1651]. A smart phrase with automatic SBP calculation: 17% to 62% [1662]. A template and laminated reminders: skin isolation 80% to 100% [2740].
fix_that_fails: Education alone gave little change: exsanguination 9.8%, skin 5.2% [1651]. EPR roll-out without a template dropped compliance to 17% [1662]. Teaching, checklist and posters left most items under 50%; time stayed at 56% [1740]. Pressures within standard did not improve with the proforma (13.0% lower limb) [1651].
consultant_advice: Well audited, with a known fix: a mandatory electronic template. Don't repeat the documentation audit. Audit the pressures actually used, cuff sizing and paediatric pressures, which stay poor even when documentation improves.
